sections.html:
Lewiston is the Nez Perce County seat in north central Idaho, where the Snake and Clearwater rivers meet. The 2025 estimate is 34,717 residents, up from 34,203 in the 2020 census. It anchors the Lewiston, ID-WA metropolitan area, which takes in Nez Perce County and Asotin County, Washington, and Clarkston sits just across the state line.

Agriculture, paper, timber products and light manufacturing drive the economy, along with ammunition makers CCI and Speer Bullet. The city is also the regional center for transportation, retail and health care, and Lewis-Clark State College is in town. Most buyers are local or from the surrounding area, though some come from across the river in Washington. Idaho law and Nez Perce County offices govern the sale of an Idaho house wherever the buyer lives. Owners who inherit a house or move away for work often need to sell without months of repairs and showings.

Lewiston is split between a low river valley and a high plateau, and the two feel like different markets. Downtown sits between 740 and 780 feet, only slightly above the water, and the terrain climbs fast away from the rivers. The lowest point in Idaho is on the Snake River in Lewiston, where it meets the Clearwater.

The mostly residential southern half of the city is called the Orchards. It sits at about 1,400 feet on a plateau and takes its name from the fruit orchards that once covered it. The area was annexed in late 1969, which nearly doubled the city's population and doubled its area. Little sign of orchards remains, though many backyards still hold fruit trees. The airport is on the western edge of the plateau.

  • River and downtown areas: lower elevation, closer to the rivers, older street grid.
  • The Orchards: higher plateau, mostly residential, reached from downtown by the Thain Grade road.

If your house is near the river, ask your insurer about flood and drainage exposure. Lenders check flood maps for financed buyers, and a cash buyer will weigh the same risks when pricing.

sections.h2: Heat, snow and the reservoir failure
sections.html:
Short, mostly mild winters and hot, dry summers mean heat does the most wear on roofs, siding and cooling equipment. A typical year brings 12.31 inches of precipitation and 10.5 inches of snow. Afternoons reach 90 degrees Fahrenheit about 42 times a year and 100 degrees about 7.7 times. The growing season lasts 195 days, and the record high is 117 degrees, set July 27, 1939. The last year without a 100-degree day was 1995. Check air conditioning age and attic ventilation before you list.

One local event is worth knowing about. The city's high reservoir failed on January 18, 2023, releasing roughly three million gallons of water and causing flooding. If your house sits in an affected area, keep repair and insurance records handy for buyers.

The City of Lewiston has adopted current building codes, and permits are required for covered work. The codes can be viewed free on the International Code Council website, and the city publishes a fee schedule and zoning application information.

Remodel work done without a permit may be spotted by a buyer's inspector. Ask the city what is on record before you list. School assignment is a frequent buyer question. Lewiston Independent School District No. 1 runs seven elementary schools, two junior high schools and two high schools.

Nez Perce County sends the tax bill for Lewiston houses. Bills are mailed each November. Pay half by December 20 and the balance by June 20 of the following year. Treasurer's office: 1230 Main Street, Lewiston, phone 208-799-3030, with online payment available.

As of January 1 the assessor sets value at 100% of market less exemptions, and nothing in law limits how far one value can move. A district's property tax budget, though, can rise only 3% a year unless voters approve more or new construction and annexation expand the base.

These are the statewide dates for Idaho counties.

Owners who live in the house get 50% off the value of the home and up to one acre, capped at $125,000. The benefit ends at a sale, so the buyer files again. Before closing, have the title company prorate taxes and verify that the first half is paid.

sections.h2: What a Lewiston seller must disclose
sections.html:
Anyone selling one to four unit residential property, including a rental the owner does not occupy, must complete a condition form under Idaho Code 55-2504. Sales, exchanges, installment contracts and options to purchase all count.

Idaho Code 55-2505 sets out the exemptions: court-ordered transfers, estate transfers (by a fiduciary or from a decedent), transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and sales by an heir who has not occupied the house within the past year. Many Lewiston sellers inherited their house, so check these exemptions with an Idaho attorney or title officer. A family home held for years can qualify.

Exempt or not, expect questions on the roof, furnace, water heater, plumbing and known leaks. Buyers need those answers to set a price.

sections.h2: Preparing a Lewiston house for buyers
sections.html:
Start with the location story. A buyer in the valley wants to hear about flood maps and drainage. A buyer on the Orchards plateau wants to hear about lot size, fruit trees and distance to the airport. Match your description to the area.

Next, put together paperwork that heads off questions: the latest tax statement, permits for remodel work, and repair and insurance records if your street felt the 2023 reservoir flooding. Add how old the roof, furnace, water heater and air conditioner are, because an inspector will price each.

Photos help more than most owners expect. Show the view if the house sits on the plateau above the valley, and show the yard in its best season, especially if fruit trees remain from the old orchards.

Finally, decide your timeline. Light snow and long warm seasons make Lewiston easy to show for much of the year, so a listing can work well if you have time. If an estate, a move or a repair bill sets a firm date, a direct offer may fit better. Either way, line up the title company early, since inherited houses often need extra signatures and court paperwork.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of a Lewiston house works
sections.html:
Since a cash buyer needs no loan, closing follows the title work and your chosen date. Send the address and condition details, look over an offer, and let a title company clear title and close.

  1. Describe who lives there, any liens or back taxes and the repairs needed.
  2. Compare the offer with a listing's costs: repairs, commissions and months of upkeep.
  3. Choose a closing date that fits your move or the estate timeline.

You owe nothing if you turn an offer down. For some owners a listing nets more, and a local agent can help you compare.

faqs.q: What is the population of Lewiston, Idaho?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 34,717 residents. The 2020 census counted 34,203.

faqs.q: When are Nez Perce County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half or full payment is due December 20, and the second half is due June 20 of the following year.

faqs.q: Which county office do I contact about my Lewiston property tax bill?
faqs.a: Contact the Nez Perce County Treasurer at 1230 Main Street in Lewiston, phone 208-799-3030. For a value question, start with the county assessor.

faqs.q: What are the Orchards in Lewiston?
faqs.a: The Orchards is the mostly residential southern half of the city on a plateau about 1,400 feet up. It was annexed in late 1969 and is named for the fruit orchards that once covered it.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems when selling a Lewiston house?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Idaho Code 55-2504 requires a property condition disclosure form for one to four unit residential property, with exemptions in 55-2505 such as estate transfers.
